Credentials viewed as important for implementing federal rebate programs include Building Performance Institute (BPI), Air Conditioning Contractors of America (ACCA), North American Technician Excellence (NATE), and Residential Energy Services Network (RESNET) certifications. 5 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 3 Survey Methodology The objective of this study is to examine why building efficiency contractors decide to train, upskill, and hire new workers, and understand how these decisions are made, including what information influences decision makers, where they access that information, and what their perceptions are of the different training and hiring pathways available to them. Contractors are a key stakeholder in the workforce development ecosystem; understanding their decision-making processes can inform policies, programs, and strategies to increase the energy efficiency workforce and more effectively connect training resources and trainees to contractors. Following the literature review, the research team worked with an internal research advisory group to frame the scope of the research and formulate survey questions, with the goal of ensuring that questions would be relevant to the target audience. The research plan and survey design were reviewed and approved by the Central U.S. Department of Energy Institutional Review Board to meet standards and ethics for human-subjects research. 3.1 Participants The target population for this survey was contractors and contractor businesses whose primary work is completing energy performance improvement projects in residential buildings, including single-family houses, manufactured housing, and multifamily buildings. Responses were received from contractors who also work in commercial buildings. Responses were allowable from business owners, decision makers, and employees of the following contractor groups: HVAC/R mechanics, installers, or technicians; electricians; insulation workers (floor, ceiling, and walls); plumbers; building performance specialists; weatherization technicians; general contractors; remodeling contractors; solar installers; and energy auditors, HERS raters, and energy consultants.
